bifurcation.note: This verdict judges whether named mechanisms act on the running world — where a body stands, whether a per-frame field has a consumer, whether an occlusion test fires. It cites screenshots as measurements of those mechanisms, not as art-direction or fidelity comparisons against a reference, so neither visual axis is engaged and no visual reference was consulted.

the sibling sweep's tripwire is a name-grep: deleting the call site leaves 3 mentions and exit 0; gutting the method body leaves 2 mentions, both prose, and exit 0. Only a full rename goes red.

reference_items.why_not_ten: Axis mapping, stated because two checks here do NOT map 1:1 onto the item's five axes and the aggregator would otherwise fix the min at 0. Consumer named: PASS at the 10 band — game/src/render/renderer.js:742, called at 1142. Coupling measured: PASS — perturbing charOpacity to 0.5, 0.25 and 0.0 changes the player's materials and then removes the body from the frame, on an RTX A5000. Hand-feed audit: not exercised by this piece. Instrumentation honesty scores at the 6 band and NOT at 0: the item's 0 condition is "undeclared trace-only fields presented as implementation", and this piece did the opposite — it declared the failure, named the consumer it built, and recorded its three amber routes by hand. The check named tripwire-can-fail-for-a-plausible-regression is a finding about the sweep TOOL, not about an undeclared field, and it is the biggest gap of this verdict rather than a zero on this axis. Harness fidelity is the binding axis and scores 4: first-ten.mjs drives the shipping entry point, so it is not the "partial harness with no VERIFY" the axis was written for, but it published two columns as null for eleven consecutive stops from a field-name mismatch with no check that would notice. min-over-axes therefore gives 4.

score.note: overall_0_10 is the minimum over the SIX NAMED PIECE AXES in section 7 of the verdict markdown (D3 7.5, charOpacity 8.0, D2 8.0, D1 5.0, reporting honesty 9.0, instrument integrity 4.0), which is the aggregation the dispatch asked for and the one that describes this piece's own work. It is deliberately NOT the minimum over reference_items, which is 2: RI-CAM01 is capped by a triggered automatic fail (the buried camera) that the piece explicitly did not claim to close and that this critic agrees is open. Scoring the piece at 2 for a defect it honestly filed as unfixed would punish the honesty this project is trying to buy. Both numbers are on the page so a reader can take whichever they want.

biggest_gap.what: tools/render/consumption-sweep.mjs tests whether a field NAME is MENTIONED anywhere under game/src/render/, not whether it is consumed. Deleting the call site this._applyCharacterFade(c) leaves 3 mentions and exit 0; gutting the method body to `return;` leaves 2 mentions, both inside its own doc comment, and exit 0. Only renaming every occurrence — the one deletion nobody performs by accident — reaches exit 1. The piece's own control for the tool is that single trivial arm.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The one regression guard this piece leaves behind cannot see the regression it exists to catch, so the camera fade can silently stop running and every dashboard stays green — which is the exact failure that produced the charOpacity defect in the first place.

remedy.action: Make the sweep a consumption test rather than a mention test, in tools/render/consumption-sweep.mjs only. Minimum viable change: strip block comments, line comments and string literals from each render/ source before matching, so prose can never satisfy the tripwire; then require the surviving match to sit on a call path reachable from Renderer.render(). Cheapest sufficient form of the second half, if the static call-path walk proves awkward, is a live arm: boot the game through tools/lib/browser.mjs, perturb the field on the sim object, render one shipping frame and require some observable to change — the machinery already exists in tools/harness/critic-first-ten-play.mjs phase `fade`. Do not add a second tool; extend this one. Preserve the existing VISUAL/INTERNAL/AMBER classification and the three hand-checked amber routes, which are correct and were checked by hand.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run the three delete-the-fix arms in corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/first-ten-minutes/consumption-sweep-delete-the-fix.log on a sparse copy. Required: arm A exit 1, arm B exit 1, arm C exit 1, and the unmodified shipped tree exit 0. Three red arms and one green; today it is one red and three green. Publish the four exit codes.

corpus_extended.note: Appendix A, appended. The repository's standard way of counting one actor's on-screen pixels — render twice and swap that actor's materials to colorWrite:false — leaks between actors on this build, because render/actor.js:473 hands the same armour material instances to every actor. It reported 6485 px for a body that is 262 px. The appendix records the failure, the corrected method (toggle root.visible), the two caveats that come with it (it removes the cast shadow, and it is not a substitute for the see-through measurement), and the general rule: a probe that mutates shared state to isolate one object is only valid if the state is private. Nobody live had declared the file (node tools/ownership.mjs --for). No threshold or weight was changed; the addition is purely additive.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is false and the shortfalls are named in section 9 of the verdict markdown. Not done: no settlement other than Lilmoth was entered, so the piece's own open question about the door derivation in a town whose buildings ring the centre is still open; the character fade was demonstrated by perturbation but was never photographed in motion against a wall, so the picture the builder said it owed is still owed; and the fight arm was captured but not judged, being outside the piece's claims. Two further honesty notes. My first probe hid actors by setting material colorWrite:false, which render/actor.js:473's shared armour materials made contaminate the player as well; it is filed as negative evidence and the corrected probe toggles root.visible instead, which also removes the cast shadow and makes my percentages body-plus-shadow where the builder's are body only. And I initially reported that D1 did not reproduce on GPU; that was wrong, caused by a look-around phase in my own harness leaving about 24 degrees of residual yaw so the player walked past the occluder, and it is retracted in section 6d. As a critic I read the production sources under judgement and wrote none of them; the only code I authored is tools/harness/critic-first-ten-play.mjs and the delete-the-fix arms, which ran on a sparse copy outside the repository. Corpus: RI-MTH04 gained Appendix A, because this review hit a real edge of the corpus — the standard actor-pixel method is unsound on this build and nothing written down said so.
